newsitem.title: UK: LME ups 1997 charges to fund expenditure increases.
newsitem.headline: LME ups 1997 charges to fund expenditure increases.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange (LME) has raised 1997 charges to members to fund "substantial" expenditure increases likely to arise from the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the metals markets.

In a notice to all members dated December 20 the LME said it has raised contract levies on "normal" futures and options trades, annual subscriptions, and listed warehouse and LME warranted metal charges.

"We have budgeted for substantial increases in expenditure in 1997, in anticipation of the need to accomodate the likely financial impact of the SIB's proposals arising out of its review of the metals markets," the notice said.
The increases would be necessary despite buoyant turnover on the LME, with year-to-date turnover this year on a par with volumes achieved in the comparable 1995 period, the LME added.

With effect from January 1 1997, contract levies on "normal" futures and options trades will increase to nine pence per lot per side from six pence for ring dealing members and to 24 pence from 15 pence per lot per side for other clearing members.
Annual subscriptions would be increased for all member categories except individual and honorary members.
Ring dealing members and associate broker clearing members will pay 30,000 stg annually in 1997 from 24,000 stg in 1996.
Associate broker member subscriptions will rise to 15,500 stg from 12,500 while associate trade clearing member subscriptions will go up to 9,500 stg from 7,500.
Associate trade members, authorised dealers, ordinary clerks and press affiliates also face higher subcription charges next year, the LME said.

The LME also raised annual warehouse listing fees to 1,800 stg per warehouse company per good delivery point from 1,500 stg. The listing fee for additional warehouses increased to 1,500 stg from 1,250 stg.
The LME warranted metal fee is also increased to 18 pence per metric tonne per annum from 15 pence.
